title: Cloudflare's CDN terms say large files need a paid Cloudflare product, and Pexi sends a 6.8 MB file to every install through the free CDN
evidence: https://www.cloudflare.com/service-specific-terms-application-services/ (page says Last updated September 28, 2026), heading 'Content Delivery Network (Free, Pro, or Business)'. Verbatim pieces: 'Cloudflare's content delivery network (the "CDN") Service can be used to cache and serve web pages and websites.' / 'Unless you are an Enterprise customer, Cloudflare offers specific Paid Services' / '(e.g., the Developer Platform, Images, and Stream) that you must use in order to serve video' / 'and other large files via the CDN.' / 'Cloudflare reserves the right to disable or limit your access to or use of the CDN' / ', if you use or are suspected of using the CDN without such Paid Services to serve video' / 'or a disproportionate percentage of pictures, audio files, or other large files.' / 'We will use reasonable efforts to provide you with notice of such action.' (that last one fetched in an earlier read; the fetch tool caps quotes at 125 characters so the paragraph is joined from pieces). The clause sets no size threshold, so whether a 6.8 MB application/octet-stream file is a 'large file' is not defined anywhere I could find. app/src/pack-route.ts:116-122 serves pack-*.bin.br as application/octet-stream, 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable', through relay.anjiawenda.com. By bytes the pack is most of a new install's traffic (a scan answer is a small JSON body; assumed, not measured). Cache side is fine: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/default-cache-behavior/ 'Free, Pro and Business customers have a limit of 512 MB.' and BIN is a default-cached extension; I did NOT confirm live that the versioned .bin address is now answered from the edge (needs the invite header, and the round limit forbids spending it).
fix: Two routes. (a) Cheapest and honest: before launch ask Cloudflare support in writing whether one 6.8 MB cached .bin per install on a paid-app API zone is acceptable; keep the answer. (b) Move the pack bytes to a product the clause names (Developer Platform, e.g. R2 plus a Worker route on relay.anjiawenda.com/api/pack/*), which keeps the same address so the installed app is unchanged. Option (b) pricing not checked (assumed: a few USD a month at most).
fix_cost: (a) 30 minutes, $0; (b) about half a day of work, assumed under US$5 a month
dup_of: none (R12 and R40 mention Cloudflare limits; the CDN large-file clause is not on any list)

title: The free plan is described as hobby-only and can be ended at Cloudflare's sole discretion; Pro changes the wording but not the SLA, the large-file clause or the termination right
evidence: https://www.cloudflare.com/plans/network-cdn.md : Free 'For personal or hobby projects that aren't business-critical.'; Pro '$20' a month billed annually or '$25/mo billed monthly', 'For professional websites that aren't business-critical.'; Business '$200/mo billed annually, or $250/mo billed monthly', 'For small businesses operating online.'; SLA row: Business and Contract 100%, Pro shown as a dash (no SLA). https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/ (title 'Cloudflare Self-Serve Subscription Agreement', 'Last Updated September 12, 2025'): s2.6 'We may offer free or trial versions of the Services ("Free Services") from time to time.' / '(c) termination of the Free Service by Cloudflare in our sole discretion.' / 'We will have no liability for any harm or damage arising out of or in connection with any Free Services.'; 'THE SERVICE ARE MADE AVAILABLE TO YOU ON AN "AS IS" AND "AS AVAILABLE" BASIS'; 'We may at our sole discretion terminate your user account or Suspend or terminate your use or access to the Service at any time'; s2.2.1(b) 'create an undue burden on the Services or the networks'. The CDN clause heading is 'Free, Pro, or Business', so Pro gets the same large-file wording. Pexi is a paid subscription app (0 purchases so far), so 'hobby' and 'not business-critical' do not describe it once Plus sells.
fix: Do not treat Pro as the fix: it costs US$20 to US$25 a month and still has no uptime promise and the same termination right; it only makes the plan name match a professional site. Business (US$200 a month) is the first tier with an SLA and is not worth it at 19 phones. The real protection is not depending on one free account: keep a written plan for the host moving off Cloudflare (domain stays at Cloudflare registrar, DNS can point elsewhere).
fix_cost: Pro US$20 to 25 a month (about CAD 28 to 35 at an assumed 1.40); not recommended on its own
dup_of: R40 and external-08 name free-plan termination; NEW: the exact plan wording, the Pro and Business prices and that Pro adds no SLA

title: No separate Tunnel terms exist; Pexi's traffic falls under the Self-Serve agreement and the CDN clause
evidence: https://www.cloudflare.com/service-specific-terms-zero-trust-services (Last updated September 28, 2026): fetched, no section on Tunnel, cloudflared or Argo Tunnel; the only caps are on Gateway DNS queries (s2.3, 150,000 per seat). https://www.cloudflare.com/service-specific-terms-application-services/ : same, no Tunnel section. https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/ states no price and no limits. So no tunnel-specific bandwidth or content rule found. An HTTP hostname that is proxied through a tunnel is still served by the CDN service, so the CDN clause above applies to it (inference, assumed).
fix: None. Note: a search for tunnel terms with a Cloudflare account on a real plan page was not possible from here.

title: The repo does not say which internet provider Jamin uses; if it is Rogers, its written terms forbid running a server and forbid commercial use of the service
evidence: grep of docs/ and mac/ for Rogers, Bell, Telus, Fido, Virgin, Videotron, Shaw, Cogeco, ISP, residential, home internet found no provider name (only unrelated hits such as 'Century 21 v Rogers' case law). SETUP.md gives only 'upload about 234 Mbps' (a figure from the repo's setup note; I did not re-measure). ROGERS (read from Rogers' own PDF, https://assets.ctfassets.net/8utyj17y1gom/3f94cg1SUOoZNof6HbT49z/6752aaaa023c723d7da34097f9bed439/Rogers_Terms_of_Service_and_Other_Important_Information.pdf , marked '04/25', Acceptable Use Policy): 'xvi. operate a server in connection with the Services, including, without limitation, mail, news, file, gopher, telnet, chat, Web, or host configuration servers, multimedia streamers or multi-user interactive forums;' and 'ix. use, reproduce, distribute, sell, resell or otherwise exploit the Services or content we provide or which you obtain through the Services for any commercial purposes;' BELL (Bell Cable Internet Terms of Service, file name dated 20230930, https://www.bell.ca/Styles/all_languages/all_regions/pdf/TOS_Bell%20Cable%2020230930%20ROC-EN.pdf, read as text): no server or hosting clause found by searching for server, residential, business, commercial; the closest lines are 'resell, transfer or share the Services, with or without fees' and 'interfere with our networks, including preventing use by others, such as when your use is disproportionate or inconsistent with ordinary usage patterns'. TELUS: its own pages returned 403 to me; only a search snippet (secondhand, assumed) says the Fair Use Policy effective 2024-11-25 lists 'Operation (i.e., hosting) of servers for services such as email, web, news, chat, or other similar services' as prohibited, with unclear scope for home internet. A tunnel does not change these clauses: they restrict what the account is used for, not which ports are open; a tunnel only makes the use harder for the provider to see (assumed).
fix: Jamin to say which provider and plan; if Rogers or Telus, treat 'home internet' as a launch risk (loss of service with no notice period promised) and move the host (see the replacement finding). If Bell or another, ask the provider in writing or accept the 'ordinary usage patterns' risk. Do not rely on the tunnel as cover.
fix_cost: 5 minutes to name the provider; a move costs about CAD 8 to 35 a month
dup_of: R03 and R12 name home internet; NEW: no provider is named anywhere, and Rogers's written server and commercial-use clauses

title: Ten ways the laptop takes Pexi down, and none has a measured recovery time (all drills say 'never')
evidence: docs/readiness/DRILLS.md lines 205-212: Summary log 'Last run' = 'never' for drills 1 (alarm), 2 (reboot), 3 (restore) and the rest; the 'Minutes to 200' cells at lines 48 and 66 are empty. Recovery figures below are therefore documented estimates or one observed event, not measurements. (1) Flat battery or power cut: observed once, 2026-11-18, about 2 hours down (SETUP.md); RUNBOOK R04 says the jobs are LaunchAgents and 'nothing starts without a login', so after power returns it stays down until someone logs in (hours; Jamin at home or Tailscale cannot help before login; assumed whether auto-login is on today, the boot-survival script mac/10-boot-survival.sh is still on the needs-jamin list, needs-jamin.md:195). (2) macOS update or crash reboot: same as (1). (3) Lid shut or sleep: mac/06-verify-no-sleep.sh exists, never reported run (assumed). (4) Server process dies: launchd KeepAlive, 'kill -9 recovery seconds' is a blank cell in DRILLS drill 6 (assumed seconds). (5) Memory pressure: 85 MB free, 264 MB swap, load test broke at 16 users (SETUP.md, one run); a stall or kill with no automatic relief; recovery is a restart, minutes once someone notices. (6) Tunnel or Cloudflare fault (530): 2026-11-18 17:50 UTC, found by the Mac checker not the GitHub alarm (REGISTER item 2); duration not recorded. (7) Home internet or router fault, or the provider ending service: no second path; waits for the provider (unknown hours to days). (8) Disk death, theft, water: RUNBOOK R07 'expect a day or more'; no off-site copy (SHIN_RESTIC_REPOSITORY blank, SETUP.md); the 4.1 GB catalogue also exists on Jamin's PC (mac/04-catalogue-acquire.md:11-14) but shopper data does not exist anywhere else; restore never rehearsed. (9) Bad deploy: auto on push every 30 s, rollback by mailbox message to a Mac Claude session or by hand on the Mac (RUNBOOK R09); never drilled. (10) Nobody at the laptop after 2027-05-03 for anything needing hands (R06). Also: every one of these needs the same single person.
fix: Run drills 2 and 3 once and write the minutes in; add a second path for (1), (2) and (7): either a host in a data centre or at least a UPS plus boot-survival script plus a cellular fallback. Until measured, quote no recovery time to anyone.
fix_cost: drill 2: 30 to 45 minutes; drill 3: 2 to 3 hours (DRILLS.md estimates); host move below
dup_of: gap 93, R03, R04, R07, R09; NEW: the consolidated list, the fact that no recovery time has ever been measured, and that a ranking by time gives home internet and power as the two with no fix path

title: Replacement hosts: 4 GB memory VPS in Canada cost about CAD 6 to 34 a month; one of the cheapest is in Quebec
evidence: Prices read on each vendor page 2026-11-21. OVHcloud VPS-1, https://www.ovhcloud.com/en-ca/vps/ : '2 vCores, 4 GB RAM, 40 GB SSD NVMe', 'From $6.20 /month' (page selector is Canada (en); the page's own data has currencyCode CAD, so CAD; tax and commitment not stated); location: https://www.ovhcloud.com/en-ca/vps/vps-canada/ says 'datacentre located in Canada', a search snippet says the French page names Beauharnois, Quebec (secondhand, city not on the page I read). DigitalOcean Basic Droplet 4 GiB, https://www.digitalocean.com/pricing/droplets : '2 vCPUs, 80 GiB SSD, $24.00/month' USD, Toronto is listed among its datacenters (plan-by-region not stated); about CAD 34 at an assumed 1.40. Akamai (Linode) Shared CPU 4 GB, https://www.akamai.com/cloud/pricing/cpu : 2 vCPU, 80 GB, '$24.00' USD, about CAD 34; Toronto not confirmed on the pages I read (assumed). AWS Lightsail 4 GB general purpose, https://aws.amazon.com/lightsail/pricing/ : '$24' USD, 2 vCPU, 80 GB SSD (IPv6-only $20); the page did not mention a Canada region; ca-central-1 is Montreal, Quebec (from memory, not checked). Vultr: its own page returned 403; a third-party listing (valebyte.com) shows 2 vCPU 4 GB in Toronto at '$20' USD, indicative only. Hetzner, https://www.hetzner.com/cloud/ : locations Germany, Finland, Singapore, Hillsboro and Ashburn in the US, 'No' Canadian location; from EUR 5.49 excluding VAT. Memory: server peaked near 2 GB (gap 93), so 4 GB leaves headroom for the 4.1 GB catalogue file cache only partly; the 8 GB tier (OVH VPS-2 '$11.64', 75 GB) is the safer choice for the load-test day. Disk: backups skip the catalogue (mac/07-backup.sh:19), but the weekly price refresh needs 6 GB free (mac/hammer-refresh.sh:49), so 20 GB is tight; 40 to 80 GB is what these plans ship with anyway.
fix: Pick the host after naming the provider question above. If the policy sentence 'outside Quebec' is to stay true, pick Toronto (DigitalOcean TOR1) over a Quebec site. Whichever is chosen, rerun the load test there and record free memory before the move.
fix_cost: CAD 6 to 12 a month (OVH VPS-1 or VPS-2) or about CAD 34 (US vendors with a Toronto site); 1 to 2 days to port (gap 93)

title: Moving to a rented host changes the privacy policy in three ways nobody has listed, one of them already wrong for the off-site backup
evidence: Policy, https://xu826jamin.github.io/pexi/privacy.html (effective 2026-11-21), verbatim: 'Pexi's server and most of these services are outside Quebec, and some are outside Canada' / 'including in the United States and the European Union, where privacy law differs.' / 'Pexi shares user data only with the services named here' / 'Server backups drop the copy within about 15 days.' / 'Backups of the server can hold a copy for longer until they are replaced.' NEW 1: the policy names no hosting company because today there is none; a rented host processes every scan and device id, so it becomes a service provider that must be named (the Law 25 transfer assessment itself is already a gap item and is not repeated here). NEW 2: if the host is in Quebec (OVH Beauharnois, AWS Montreal, both Quebec per the host finding) the sentence 'outside Quebec' becomes false; a Toronto host keeps it true; assumed that the laptop is outside Quebec today (McMaster, Ontario). A Canadian host does not change 'some are outside Canada' because Cloudflare, Anthropic and RevenueCat stay. NEW 3, independent of any move: mac/14-offsite-backup.sh:21 and :121 keep 14 daily, 8 weekly and 6 monthly snapshots ('restic forget --tag shin-nightly --keep-daily 14 --keep-weekly 8 --keep-monthly 6 --prune'), so a deleted shopper's data stays in the off-site copy for up to about 6 months, against the published 'about 15 days'. Grep of docs/security-check/legal-review-2026-11-17.md, FINDINGS.md, REGISTER.md and the gaps list for restic or retention of weekly or monthly snapshots found nothing on this.
fix: Set the off-site retention to what the policy says (for example keep-daily 14 and no weekly or monthly) or change the policy sentence; name the host in the provider list when the move happens; choose a Toronto site or reword 'outside Quebec'. redelete-requests.mjs already re-applies deletions to a restored copy (R58), which covers the restore side only.
fix_cost: 10 minutes for the retention flags; 15 minutes of policy text on the move
dup_of: R50 and the Law 25 gap item cover policy drift and transfers; NEW: the host-provider listing, the Quebec sentence and the 6-month off-site retention

title: Gap 93's list of what must be ported misses the catalogue and pack copy, secrets, off-site backup, logs, the alert path, outside-address limits and the cutover
evidence: Checked against mac/launchd-daemons/*.plist, mac/launchd/*.plist, mac/deploy/*.mjs, app/src/watch.ts, mac/config.env.example. CONFIRMED in gap 93: ten LaunchDaemons (server, checker, backup, offsite, integrity, logrotate, hammer, restoretest, expiry, deadman) plus the tunnel; mac/deploy/deployer.mjs:217-235 restarts through launchctl and uses lsof; mac/deploy/lib.mjs:661-662 'sudo -n /bin/launchctl'; mac/deploy/util.mjs:158 hard-codes PATH '/opt/homebrew/bin:...'. ADDED (not in gap 93): (a) mac/expiry-check.mjs:26 reads the macOS login keychain with 'security find-certificate', Mac only. (b) app/src/watch.ts:448 and :478 return null off darwin for pmset and fdesetup, so the health report loses power and disk-encryption fields (harmless, but the alerts that read them go quiet). (c) THE CATALOGUE AND PACKS ARE NOT DELIVERED BY A PUSH: .gitignore line 19 'catalogue/data/'; mac/04-catalogue-acquire.md:197-198 copies catalogue.db (4,140,003,328 bytes plus a -wal file at the time written) and both pack files from the Windows PC over rsync; a new host needs that copy plus a checksum, and the WAL trap in that file (copying catalogue.db alone silently drops recent writes). The PC copy is the only other copy and it is live-written. (d) SECRETS: config.env.example holds ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, SHIN_INVITE_CODE, the Gemini key, App Store Connect key id, issuer and key file, the restic password file, the tunnel credential JSON; each has to be copied to the new host over a safe path and the old ones rotated if the laptop is retired; the Mac Claude sessions that run with permission checks off hold them today. (e) OFF-SITE BACKUP: mac/14-offsite-backup.sh exists, SHIN_RESTIC_REPOSITORY is blank, so a rented host does not by itself give a copy outside the host; a provider snapshot or restic to a different company is still needed. (f) LOGS AND PRIVACY FILES: SHIN_LOG_DIRS and 16-rotate-logs.sh (keep 14 days), the request log in /Users/worker/shin-privacy/request-log.csv and the photos and shutter folders under SHIN_DATA_DIR must move with their rules (the 90-day log line in the policy). (g) DEPLOY AND ALERT PATH: the checker polls GitHub every 30 s and reports through the Claude mailbox (SHIN_DEPLOY_REPORT=mailbox, SHIN_MAILBOX_DIR=/Users/worker/claude-mailbox, config.env.example:49-51), 'deploy: pin <sha>' arrives by mailbox (RUNBOOK); a host with no Claude session has no pin path and no mail alert, only the GitHub Actions probe. (h) OUTSIDE ADDRESS: Open Food Facts (12 a minute) and Overpass now see a home address; from a data-centre address they may rate-limit or block differently (assumed, not tested). (i) THE CUTOVER WITH THE SAME ADDRESS: the app talks only to relay.anjiawenda.com (SETUP.md), so no app update; options are run cloudflared with the same tunnel credential on the new host and stop the Mac's, or point the relay DNS record at the host. SQLite is single-writer, so the order is: stop the Mac server, copy scans.db and the other shopper files with WAL checkpointed (mac/checkpoint-wal.mjs exists), start the new host, check health, switch. Never two live copies (assumed). Expect minutes of write outage and one rehearsal first. (j) THE 6.8 MB PACK: whichever route is taken for the Cloudflare large-file clause (see the first finding) must be done on the new host too.
fix: Add (a) to (j) to gap 93 and order the port: secrets and catalogue first, a rehearsal cutover on a throwaway hostname, then the real one in a quiet hour.
fix_cost: about 1 to 2 days plus one rehearsal (assumed)
dup_of: gap 93; NEW: items a to j above
